name: LangChain
summary: A Python agent and LLM application framework that composes provider-independent model interfaces, runnable units, tools, messages, and agent harnesses, with LangGraph providing lower-level orchestration.

features.name: Provider-independent model interface
features.description: The official README describes standard interfaces for models, embeddings, vector stores, and integrations, while the fixed source contains the core message and runnable packages. The claim is about the abstraction boundary, not identical provider behavior.
benefits: Allows model and integration choices to change behind shared application interfaces
Separates application composition from individual provider adapters
costs: Provider-specific capabilities and error semantics still leak through adapters
A shared interface does not guarantee equivalent latency, output, or safety properties

features.name: Runnable composition and execution
features.description: The fixed Runnable source defines a unit of work that can be invoked, batched, streamed, transformed, and composed. It documents sequential RunnableSequence and concurrent RunnableParallel composition, plus configuration for tracing and runtime behavior.
benefits: Supports reusable pipelines with sequential and concurrent composition
Makes execution and tracing configuration explicit at the runnable boundary
costs: Composition changes data shape and concurrency semantics
Batching and parallel execution introduce resource and ordering concerns

features.name: Typed tool-call boundary
features.description: The fixed tool source defines BaseTool as the interface for agent actions, including a name, description, input schema, invocation hooks, callbacks, metadata, and tool-error handling.
benefits: Makes model-to-action invocation inspectable through a named schema
Allows tool errors and callbacks to be handled without collapsing the entire agent run
costs: Tool descriptions and schemas become part of the model-facing contract
External effects remain application-specific and may be repeated or partially completed

features.name: Agent harness over orchestration layer
features.description: Current official documentation describes create_agent as a configurable harness around model, tools, prompt, and middleware, and states that LangChain agents are built on LangGraph for durable execution, persistence, and human-in-the-loop support. The LangChain repository itself remains the fixed source for the core framework boundary; the LangGraph relationship is documented ecosystem context.
benefits: Composes agent behavior from model, tool, prompt, and middleware choices
Separates a high-level agent API from lower-level orchestration capabilities
costs: Middleware and orchestration state expand the control-flow surface
Durability or persistence claims depend on the LangGraph/runtime configuration and are not unconditional LangChain guarantees

mathematical_views.model: Runnable algebra over typed inputs and outputs
mathematical_views.question: How do sequential, parallel, batched, streamed, and transformed runnable executions compose?
assumptions: A Runnable maps an input to an output or execution error
Sequence composes output-to-input edges; parallel evaluates branches over shared input
The view abstracts provider I/O and does not assume all runnables are pure

mathematical_views.question: How do model messages, tool calls, tool results, and middleware produce the next agent state?
assumptions: Tool calls are represented as named, schema-constrained actions
Tool execution may fail and return an observation according to configured handling
The view abstracts a specific model provider and does not prove policy compliance

mathematical_views.model: Abstraction refinement from harness to graph runtime
mathematical_views.question: Which properties belong to the LangChain agent harness and which require the LangGraph orchestration layer?
assumptions: The official docs distinguish LangChain create_agent from low-level LangGraph orchestration
Durability, persistence, and human-in-the-loop are treated as documented layer capabilities, not inferred from the core Runnable alone
This is a candidate architectural relation, not a proof of implementation equivalence

costs: Provider differences remain at the adapter edge

benefits: Reusable sequential and concurrent execution units
costs: Data-shape and concurrency semantics require composition discipline

benefits: Explicit model-to-action contract and error boundary
costs: Schemas and external side effects remain coupled

benefits: High-level agent API with a lower-level orchestration escape hatch
costs: Layer selection and persistence configuration affect guarantees
